# Folio Desktop: Production-Readiness, UX and Feature Report

*Prepared 12 Nov 2026 for an AI coding agent. Scope: static review of all 138 files in the upload (Tauri 2, React 18, Readium navigator, v0.1.0). Nothing was executed, so items marked \[verify\] need a quick repro before fixing.*

## 1. How to use this report

**Severity.** P0 = fix before any public release. P1 = high-impact UX, feature or performance gap. P2 = medium. P3 = polish.

**Item format.** Every item has an ID, **Where** (files), **Problem**, **Fix** and **Done when** (acceptance test). Follow the roadmap in section 10 and add a regression test for each fix.

**Hard constraints**

- Schema-1 files (manifest, meta, annotations, progress, collections, prefs) must stay byte-compatible with the mobile app. Changes are additive only. Never rename or remove fields.
- Keep the manifest-last write ordering and the per-path mutex in `fileStore.ts` and `libraryManager.ts`.
- Folio has no telemetry. Diagnostics stay local. Do not add network calls without explicit product sign-off.
- Google Drive sync and the offline dictionary were removed on purpose (decision records D-20261031-03 and D-20261031-05). Do not bring them back. Anything touching them is a product decision, not a bug.
- Design tokens are asserted against `tests/fixtures/tokens.json`. When you change a token, update the fixture in the same commit.
- The `tests/` folder and the CI workflow were not in the upload. Follow the Vitest conventions described in the README.

## 2. Executive summary

Folio is a well-structured, privacy-respecting reader with careful data handling: atomic writes, manifest-last commits, a navigation coordinator, focus-trapped dialogs and reduced-motion support. It is close to feature-complete for a v0.1. What stands between it and a production release is a short list of real defects plus a set of reading-experience gaps.

**Top 10 priorities**

1. Dark theme primary buttons are unreadable (1.86:1 contrast). P0-1.
2. Panels and dialogs re-run their focus logic on every parent render, which steals focus. The in-book search box never keeps focus. P0-2.
3. No React error boundary: any render error leaves a blank window. P0-3.
4. The error log exists but nothing writes to it, and 30+ catch blocks swallow errors silently. P0-4.
5. Rust file commands accept any absolute path on disk. P0-5.
6. File I/O commands run synchronously on the UI thread and move bytes as JSON number arrays, so imports and backups freeze the window. E1.
7. In-book search finds chapters, not matches, jumps to the chapter start and closes after one click. R1.
8. There is no "go back" after a jump, and highlights cannot be clicked to edit. R4, R5.
9. A freshly imported book sorts to the bottom of "Recently read", and the list flashes "Loading…" on every refresh. L1, L3.
10. No per-book actions, no notes export, no updater and no code signing. L4, N1, E5.

## 3. P0: Release blockers

### P0-1 Dark theme: primary buttons and danger states fail contrast

**Where:** `src/styles/tokens.css` (the `[data-theme="dark"]` block); `src/styles/components.css` (`.folio-btn--primary`, `.folio-btn--solid-danger`, `.folio-btn--danger:hover`).

**Problem:** The dark block overrides `--folio-accent` to `#A7C4A6` but never overrides `--folio-on-accent` (`#FFFDF7`). Near-white text on pale green measures 1.86:1, so every primary button in dark mode is nearly unreadable. `--folio-danger-container` and `--folio-on-danger-container` are also light-theme only, so the danger button hover (pale pink background with `#E0A09A` text) is roughly 1.7:1.

**Fix:** Add dark values: `--folio-on-accent` as a dark green (for example `#14201A`), `--folio-danger-container` as a dark red-brown (for example `#3A2220`), `--folio-on-danger-container` as a light pink (for example `#F3C9C4`). Check the `.folio-btn--solid-danger` text colour in both themes. Reuse `src/lib/contrast.ts` (`contrastRatio`, `AA_NORMAL`) to assert every text and background token pair.

**Done when:** A test parses both token blocks and asserts at least 4.5:1 for all text pairs and at least 3:1 for control borders and focus rings, in light and dark.

### P0-2 FolioPanel and FolioDialog steal focus on every parent re-render \[verify\]

**Where:** `src/components/FolioPanel.tsx` and `FolioDialog.tsx` (effect deps `[open, onClose]`). Callers in `ReaderScreen.tsx` pass inline arrow functions, for example `onClose={() => setPanel(null)}`.

**Problem:** The effect cleanup restores focus to the previously focused element and pops the modal token. The effect body then focuses the first focusable element again and pushes a new token. Because `onClose` is a new function on every render, this runs whenever the parent re-renders: on every page turn, once a second for the pace label, and on every keystroke in the in-book search (`inbookQuery` is `ReaderScreen` state). The first focusable element in a panel is the header Close button, so the search input's `autoFocus` is overridden on open and typed text loses focus. Keyboard users moving through the Contents list get reset to the top.

**Fix:** Store `onClose` in a ref that is updated every render and depend only on `[open]`. Add `data-autofocus` to the search input, the note textarea and other primary fields (`focusFirstIn` already honours it). Restore focus only when the surface actually closes.

**Done when:** A test renders a panel, focuses an input inside it, re-renders the parent with a new `onClose`, and asserts focus did not move. Typing a multi-character query in in-book search keeps focus in the input.

### P0-3 No error boundary

**Where:** `src/App.tsx`, `src/main.tsx`, `src/shell/Shell.tsx`.

**Problem:** There is no ErrorBoundary anywhere. A render exception in any screen unmounts the whole tree and leaves a blank window with no recovery other than killing the app. The reader is the most exposed screen (1,487 lines, many effects).

**Fix:** Add a root ErrorBoundary with a recovery screen: a plain-language explanation, Reload, Open log folder, Copy diagnostics. Add a second boundary around `ReaderScreen` that offers "Back to library" and flushes progress. Log through `reportError`.

**Done when:** Throwing inside any screen shows the recovery UI, reading progress is still flushed, and the error appears in the log file.

### P0-4 Errors are swallowed and the error log is never written to

**Where:** `src/lib/errorLog.ts` (`reportError` has zero callers outside this file). More than 30 `catch` blocks contain only a comment, for example in `ReaderScreen.tsx` (annotations, clipboard), `LibraryScreen.tsx`, `SettingsScreen.tsx` and `libraryUi.ts`. Unprotected awaits in `ReaderScreen.tsx`: `createAnnotation`, `saveNote`, `toggleHighlight`, and the TocPanel callbacks `onRemoveBookmark` and `onDeleteAnnotation`.

**Problem:** Failures are invisible to users and to the diagnostics log. A failed note save leaves the dialog in an inconsistent state or throws an unhandled rejection with no message. Copy-to-clipboard failure is silent.

**Fix:** Introduce `handleError(error, { context, userMessage?, toast? })` that always calls `reportError` and optionally shows a toast. Replace each silent catch deliberately: keep it silent only if truly harmless, and still log it. Wrap every annotation mutation in try/catch with an error toast and keep dialogs open with the draft intact (the pattern already used in `NotesScreen.handleEditSave`). On clipboard failure, show a toast.

**Done when:** Forcing each of those calls to reject shows a toast, writes one log line and leaves the UI usable.

### P0-5 Rust file commands are not sandboxed

**Where:** `src-tauri/src/guard.rs`, `commands/fs.rs`, `commands/zip.rs`, `commands/hash.rs`, `src-tauri/capabilities/default.json`.

**Problem:** `guard_user_path` only rejects relative paths and `..`. `fs_read`, `fs_write_atomic`, `fs_delete` (which calls `remove_dir_all`), `fs_move`, `zip_read`, `zip_write` and `sha256_file` accept any absolute path on the machine, for example `C:\Users\…`. `ensure_no_escape` exists but is dead code, and nothing checks symlinks or junctions. Custom commands are also not restricted by the capability file. If any script ever executes in the webview (a malicious EPUB, a future dependency issue) it can read, overwrite or delete arbitrary user files. The CSP blocks inline script today, which is a good first layer but is the only one.

**Fix:** Resolve and canonicalise every path and require it to stay inside the app data directory, including after resolving symlinks and Windows junctions. Allow paths outside the app dir only if they were returned by a native open or save dialog, a drag-drop event or a launch argument in this session; keep that allow-list in Tauri managed state. Add an explicit app-level permission manifest for the custom commands. Cap `zip_read` by entry count and total uncompressed bytes to stop zip bombs.

**Done when:** Rust tests prove that `/folio-library/../x`, a junction pointing outside the app dir and an arbitrary `C:\Windows\…` path are rejected, while dialog-picked and dropped paths still work. `fs_delete` can no longer remove anything outside the app dir.

## 4. P1: Reader

### R1 In-book search finds chapters, not matches

**Where:** `src/reader/readiumEngine.ts` (`getSearchIndex`, `search`); `src/components/InBookSearchPanel.tsx` (`handleSelect` calls `onClose`); `ReaderScreen.tsx`.

**Problem:** One index document is added per spine item, so a result is a chapter with only its first occurrence. The locator is the chapter href, so choosing a result lands at the start of the chapter, not at the match. The panel then closes, so you cannot step through matches, and the match is not highlighted on the page. The hint says "at least 2 characters" but nothing enforces it. The index is built synchronously on the main thread on the first query.

**Fix:** Search per occurrence. For each chapter find all matches (phrase first, then all-words) and return hits with chapter title, snippet and a text-anchored locator (quote plus 32 characters before and after) so `goAnchored` lands on the match. Group by chapter with a match count. Keep the panel open after selecting. Add Next and Previous match (Enter, Shift+Enter, F3) and a "3 of 41" counter. Highlight the active match with a temporary decoration group and clear it on close. Build the index in a Web Worker with a progress state. Enforce a 2-character minimum in the engine and the UI.

**Done when:** Searching a word that occurs 30 times in one chapter yields 30 navigable results, each landing on its occurrence with the term visibly highlighted, and the panel stays open.

### R2 Search text contains HTML entities

**Where:** `readiumEngine.ts` (`stripHtml`) versus `positions.ts` (`decodeEntities`).

**Problem:** `stripHtml` removes tags but never decodes entities. ` `, `&` and `’` stay as literal text, so snippets show "&", `nbsp` and `amp` become searchable tokens, and "don’t" written with an entity apostrophe cannot be found. `positions.ts` already has a correct decoder, so the logic is duplicated and inconsistent.

**Fix:** One shared `htmlToText()` utility (entity decoding, block elements become spaces, skip script, style and head) used by in-book search, positions, the importers and the library text index.

**Done when:** A fixture chapter containing `&`, ` ` and `’` produces clean snippets and correct matches.

### R3 Search engine performance and highlighting (in-book and library)

**Where:** `src/search/miniSearch.ts`; `LibraryScreen.tsx` (`buildSearchIndex`).

**Problem:** For each query token, `candidateIndices` scans the entire vocabulary with edit-distance checks. `score()` re-tokenises each candidate's full text, and `df()` rescans the vocabulary per candidate per token. Cost grows roughly as candidates × vocabulary × tokens, which will stall on a large book or library. `snippet()` calls `indexOf(token)` on lower-cased but unfolded text, so accent-folded matches ("cafe" for "café"), fuzzy matches and long prefix matches get no highlight or fall back to the first 120 characters. Prefix hits highlight only the query length. Matching is AND-only with no phrase queries. The library index reads every document's text file sequentially on the main thread whenever the signature changes, with no loading indicator.

**Fix:** Replace it with the real `minisearch` package (the header comment says mobile uses it), or add precomputed term frequencies, document frequencies cached per term, a sorted vocabulary with binary search for prefixes, and an offset map from normalised text back to original text for correct highlights. Add quoted phrase support. Move indexing to a Worker. For library search show "Indexing…" with progress, a "No results" state, a result count and keyboard navigation (see L9).

**Done when:** A 3 MB book searches in under 100 ms once indexed, the UI stays responsive while indexing, and accent, fuzzy and prefix hits are highlighted correctly.

### R4 No way to go back after a jump

**Where:** `src/reader/navigation.ts`; `readiumEngine.ts` (`handleLocator`); `ReaderScreen.tsx`.

**Problem:** After using Contents, search, the progress slider, a bookmark or an internal link (including footnotes) there is no way to return to where you were. Internal links call `navigator.go` directly inside `handleLocator`, bypassing the coordinator, so they get no serialisation, no outcome handling and no history.

**Fix:** Route internal links through the coordinator. Keep a short position-history stack pushed on every absolute move and link follow. Show a "Back to where you were" snackbar action and bind Alt+Left. For `epub:type="noteref"` links show a footnote popover instead of navigating.

**Done when:** After jumping via a link, Alt+Left returns to the exact previous position, and footnotes open in a popover.

### R5 Highlights are not interactive and duplicates accumulate

**Where:** `ReaderScreen.tsx` (`toggleHighlight`, `decorationsFor`); `readiumEngine.ts` (`applyDecorations`); `SelectionToolbar.tsx`.

**Problem:** Clicking an existing highlight does nothing. The only ways to change or delete it are the Reading Workspace panel or the Notes screen. `toggleHighlight` removes only when quote and colour match exactly, so selecting part of an existing highlight, or choosing another colour, adds an overlapping duplicate. The toolbar does not show which colour is already applied, and deleting has no undo.

**Fix:** Subscribe to decoration activation in the navigator and open a small popover at the highlight with: change colour, add or edit note, copy, delete (with an Undo toast). When a selection overlaps an existing highlight, update that annotation instead of adding a new one, and mark the active colour in the toolbar.

**Done when:** Clicking a highlight opens the popover, changing colour updates it in place, no overlapping duplicates appear, and a delete can be undone.

### R6 "Share as image" can share a stale quote

**Where:** `ReaderScreen.tsx` (`quoteSelection`, `shareEnabled`).

**Problem:** `quoteSelection` is set on every selection and never cleared, so after the first selection the menu item stays enabled for the whole session and shares an old passage, possibly from another chapter.

**Fix:** Put "Share" in the selection toolbar (it acts on the live selection) and clear `quoteSelection` when the selection ends or the document changes. Add "Copy with citation" (quote, title, author).

**Done when:** With no live selection the menu item is disabled, and sharing always uses the current selection.

### R7 Wrong or reused icons

**Where:** `SelectionToolbar.tsx` (Copy uses the Search icon); `ReaderChrome.tsx` ("Share as image" uses Info, "Hide controls" uses Toc); `ReaderContextMenu.tsx` ("Toggle toolbar" uses More); `TocPanel.tsx` (Edit note uses the Notes icon).

**Fix:** Add Copy, Image/Share, EyeOff and Pencil icons to `FolioIcons.tsx` and use them. Quick win, low risk.

**Done when:** No icon is reused for an unrelated action, and every icon-only button has a tooltip and an accessible name.

### R8 Panels stack on top of each other and the scrim hides the page

**Where:** `ReaderScreen.tsx` (`panel` and `inbookSearchOpen` are separate state); `FolioPanel.tsx`; `components.css` (`.folio-overlay`); `reader.css` (`.folio-reader .folio-panel`).

**Problem:** In-book search can be open together with Contents or Appearance, producing two 400 px panels in the same place with two overlays. Every panel dims the book with a 60% scrim, which defeats the Appearance panel, where the user is trying to judge size, spacing and theme on the live page.

**Fix:** Use a single `activePanel` state (`"toc" | "appearance" | "search" | null`). Make Appearance and Search non-modal docked panels (no scrim, canvas stays interactive, optionally shift the reading column so text is not covered). Contents may stay modal. Add a `modal` prop to `FolioPanel`.

**Done when:** Only one panel can be open at a time, and changing text size in Appearance shows the page unobscured.

### R9 Reading theme "System" ignores OS theme changes

**Where:** `readiumEngine.ts` (`systemDark` is read once in the constructor); `ReaderScreen.tsx` (tracks `systemDark` separately).

**Problem:** When the OS switches between light and dark while a book is open with reading theme "System", the chrome updates but the page does not.

**Fix:** Pass the resolved theme (or `systemDark`) into `applyPrefs`, or add a `setSystemDark()` method, and re-submit preferences on change.

**Done when:** Toggling the OS theme repaints the open book without reopening it.

### R10 Menus and the selection toolbar are not keyboard-accessible

**Where:** `ReaderChrome.tsx` (More menu); `ReaderContextMenu.tsx`; `SelectionToolbar.tsx`.

**Problem:** `role="menu"` is declared but focus never moves into the menu, and there is no Arrow, Home or End navigation. The context menu's `y` position is not clamped to the viewport. The selection toolbar cannot be reached from the keyboard, assumes a 260 px width and sits 48 px above the selection, so it overlaps text near the top of the page instead of flipping below.

**Fix:** Create one shared `FolioMenu` primitive (focus the first item on open, roving tabindex, type-ahead, Esc returns focus) and use it for both menus. Make the selection toolbar focusable with a shortcut and flip it below the selection when there is no room above. Clamp positions to the viewport on both axes.

**Done when:** Both menus can be fully operated with the keyboard, and no menu or toolbar can render off-screen.

### R11 Progress dock details

**Where:** `ReaderDock.tsx`, `pace.ts`, `progress.ts`, `FolioBookRow.tsx`.

**Problem:** 1% slider steps are coarse for long books. There are no chapter ticks and no label while scrubbing. Time left reads "≈ 2 h left" for anything from 90 to 150 minutes. Nothing shows time left in the chapter. Percent labels round 99.6% up to 100% for unfinished books. There is no finished state and no end-of-book screen.

**Fix:** Use finer steps (0.1%) with chapter tick marks and a tooltip showing the target chapter while dragging. Format time as "1 h 25 min left" and add "x min left in chapter". Use floor for percent labels. Add a Finished state (last position reached, or "Mark as finished"), shown as a check in the Library, with an end-of-book card (finished, back to library, next book in the collection).

**Done when:** Scrubbing shows the destination chapter, 99.6% displays as 99%, and reaching the end shows the finished card once.

### R12 Opening large books is slow and can show a false error

**Where:** `reader/epubPublication.ts` (`unzipSync`, `generatePositions`); `ReaderScreen.tsx` (`SPLASH_FAILSAFE_MS = 8000`).

**Problem:** The whole EPUB is decompressed synchronously on the main thread (and again for validation and import), every resource is held in memory, and position generation runs over every chapter. Large or image-heavy books freeze the UI and can hit the 8 second failsafe, which then reports "taking longer than expected" even though the book is still loading.

**Fix:** Use fflate's async or streaming `Unzip`, or a Worker. Decompress resources lazily on first request. Compute positions lazily or cache them in an additive cache file. Replace the fixed timer with a progress-aware one ("Still opening… 40%") and keep Retry.

**Done when:** A 40 MB illustrated EPUB opens with a responsive splash and no false error.

### R13 Keyboard model

**Where:** the keyboard effect in `ReaderScreen.tsx`; `KeyboardShortcutsDialog.tsx`.

**Problem:** Single-letter shortcuts (`t`, `m`, `f`, `?`) call `preventDefault()` even when Ctrl, Alt or Meta is held, which swallows combinations such as Ctrl+T and Ctrl+M. `f` toggles focus mode while Ctrl+F opens search, which is easy to confuse. The Escape chain duplicates what `modalStack` already does for panels and dialogs. Common shortcuts are missing: text size, previous and next chapter, theme cycle, go to position, open bookmarks.

**Fix:** Ignore plain-letter shortcuts when any modifier is down. Move Escape handling for modal surfaces fully into `modalStack`; the window handler should only handle non-modal state such as focus mode. Add Ctrl+= / Ctrl+− / Ctrl+0 for text size, `[` and `]` for chapters, and Alt+Left for history. List everything in `KeyboardShortcutsDialog`. Consider renaming focus mode to "Distraction-free" and moving it off the bare `f` key.

**Done when:** Modified key combinations are never swallowed, and every shortcut appears in the shortcuts dialog.

### R14 Two notification systems and non-accessible toast timing

**Where:** `ReaderScreen.tsx` (`navNotice`, `folio-snackbar--warn`); `shell/toasts.ts`; `ToastHost.tsx`.

**Problem:** The reader has its own snackbar, styled as a warning even for "Highlight added.", separate from the global toast host. The global host holds a single toast, so a later success can replace an unread error. Toasts auto-dismiss after 4 seconds even while hovered or focused, and have no action button, so there is no Undo. The details list uses `key={line}`, which collides on duplicate lines.

**Fix:** Delete `navNotice` and use the global host everywhere. Support a small stack (maximum 3), per-tone styling, an optional action (Undo, Back), pause on hover and focus, and keys built from id plus index.

**Done when:** An error toast is never replaced by a success toast, and Undo works from a toast.

### R15 Appearance panel is long and partly redundant

**Where:** `AppearancePanel.tsx`, `readingPrefsOptions.ts`, `readerThemes.ts`, `model/defaults.ts`.

**Problem:** Nine stacked sections with duplicated controls (quick size stepper versus slider, quick alignment versus the full section, width presets versus the width slider). The maximum font size is 32 px, which is low for low-vision readers. All typefaces are system fonts; Iowan Old Style is not installed on Windows and there is no dyslexia-friendly option. The `spread` preference (single versus double page) exists in the model but has no control, although double-page spreads are a main reason to read on a wide desktop screen. There is no "apply to all books" action and no indicator showing that a book has its own overrides.

**Fix:** Group into three tabs (Theme, Text, Layout) and remove duplicate controls. Add a Spread control. Raise the font size cap (for example 48 px, with larger steps above 32). Bundle two or three OFL-licensed fonts as woff2 (for example Literata plus a high-legibility sans); the CSP already allows `font-src 'self'`. Add "Use for all books" and a "This book has custom settings" badge.

**Done when:** All reading preferences are reachable in two clicks, spreads can be toggled, and text can be scaled to at least 48 px.

### R16 Highlight colours on dark reader themes \[verify\]

**Where:** `ReaderScreen.tsx` (`HIGHLIGHT_CSS`); `TocPanel.tsx` (`HIGHLIGHT_COLORS`); `tokens.css` (`--folio-swatch-*`).

**Problem:** Highlight colours are defined three times. On the Dark and True-black reader themes the page text is light (`#E6E3DC`, `#C8C4BC`) while the highlight background is a light pastel (`#FFF3B0`), which would give roughly 1.1:1 contrast inside the highlight.

**Fix:** One palette module with theme-aware values (translucent, darker tints for dark themes) used by page decorations, swatches and panels.

**Done when:** Highlighted text meets 4.5:1 on all four reader themes.

## 5. P1: Library and import

### L1 The list flashes "Loading…" on every refresh and loads slowly

**Where:** `store/libraryUi.ts` (`refresh`); `LibraryScreen.tsx` (the `loading ? … : …` branch).

**Problem:** `refresh()` sets `loading: true` and the screen replaces the entire list with "Loading…" after every import, delete or add-to-collection. The refresh itself is sequential: one `meta.read`, one cover `stat` and one cover `read` per book, each awaited in turn.

**Fix:** Show the loading state only when there are no rows; otherwise keep the list and show a subtle progress bar. Load metadata and covers with bounded parallelism (for example 8) and cache parsed meta by `updatedAt`. Update rows incrementally after an import instead of reloading everything.

**Done when:** Importing a book never blanks the list, and a 300-book library loads in under one second on a typical SSD.

### L2 Covers: no thumbnails, no lazy loading, no virtualisation

**Where:** `libraryUi.ts` (`loadCoverUrl`); `FolioBookRow.tsx`; `LibraryScreen.tsx`.

**Problem:** Full-size cover bytes are read and decoded as object URLs for every book on every library load, and the whole list is rendered at once. This will be sluggish and memory-heavy at a few hundred books.

**Fix:** Generate a small thumbnail (about 2× display size) at import time and store it as an additive file. Load covers lazily with IntersectionObserver. Virtualise the list and grid.

**Done when:** Memory stays flat while scrolling a 1,000-book library, and only visible covers are decoded.

### L3 "Recently read" puts new imports at the bottom

**Where:** `libraryUi.ts` (sort inside `refresh`); `LibraryScreen.tsx` (sort options).

**Problem:** The default order is `progress.updatedAt` descending, with unread books last and ordered by title. A book you just imported has no progress, so it lands at the bottom and users think the import failed. There is no "Date added" or "Progress" sort. Title sort uses plain `localeCompare`, so "Book 10" sorts before "Book 2".

**Fix:** Default to "Recent activity", defined as the later of last read and imported-at. Add Date added and Progress sorts. Use `localeCompare(undefined, { numeric: true, sensitivity: "base" })`. Briefly highlight the newly imported row and scroll to it.

**Done when:** A newly imported book appears at the top and is visibly highlighted.

### L4 No per-book actions or metadata editing

**Where:** `LibraryScreen.tsx` (never passes `onMore` to `FolioBookRow`); `model/types.ts` (`tags`, `author` and `cover` exist).

**Problem:** The only way to delete a book or add it to a collection is Select mode. Title, author, cover and tags cannot be edited, although the data model supports tags. A wrong title or author inside an EPUB cannot be corrected.

**Fix:** A right-click and "⋯" menu per book: Open, Add to collection, Edit details (title, author, cover, tags), Mark finished or unread, Show in folder, Delete (with Undo). Add tag editing and a tag filter.

**Done when:** Every per-book action is available from the row menu with keyboard access.

### L5 List only; no grid, filters or "Continue reading"

**Where:** `LibraryScreen.tsx`.

**Problem:** There is one dense list. No cover grid, no filter by kind (Book or Article), status (Unread, Reading, Finished) or tag, and no "Continue reading" shelf. Unread rows show nothing (the README promises "New"), and the percent label rounds up.

**Fix:** A persisted List and Grid toggle, filter chips, a Continue reading row (last one to three books), "New" and "Finished" badges, plus last-read date and time left on rows.

**Done when:** A user can resume their current book with one click from the Library home.

### L6 The toolbar disappears when a filter shows nothing

**Where:** `LibraryScreen.tsx` (`{count > 0 && …controls…}`).

**Problem:** `count` is the number of visible rows. If a collection filter contains no books, the Import button and the sort and filter menus all vanish, and the subtitle says "0 documents" instead of "0 of 42". Only "Show all books" remains.

**Fix:** Key the toolbar on the total number of rows and show "N of M documents" while filtered.

**Done when:** Controls stay visible for any non-empty library, whatever the filter.

### L7 "Add to collection" is a dead end and collection forms are weak

**Where:** `LibraryScreen.tsx` (addToCollection dialog); `CollectionsScreen.tsx`; `libraryManager.ts` (`createCollection`, `renameCollection`).

**Problem:** With no collections, the dialog says "No collections yet." and offers only Cancel. The create and rename dialogs do not submit on Enter and accept duplicate names and unlimited length.

**Fix:** Add an inline "New collection…" field in the picker. Use real `<form>` elements with Enter to submit, trimming, a maximum length (for example 80) and case-insensitive duplicate-name validation with an inline error.

**Done when:** A user with zero collections can create one and add books in a single flow, and pressing Enter submits.

### L8 Selection mode and deletion

**Where:** `LibraryScreen.tsx`.

**Problem:** Row checkboxes have no accessible label. Select all exists only as Ctrl+A. There is no Shift-click range. The delete dialog does not say what will be deleted. Deletion is permanent and immediate, and removes the book's notes too.

**Fix:** Label checkboxes ("Select \<title>"). Add a visible "Select all" and a sticky bulk-action bar. Support Shift-click ranges. List titles (first five plus "and N more") in the confirm dialog. Implement a soft delete: keep the data for about 10 seconds with an Undo toast before purging, or add a "Recently deleted" area.

**Done when:** A deleted book can be restored with its notes and progress within the undo window.

### L9 Library search UX

**Where:** `LibraryScreen.tsx`; `miniSearch.ts`.

**Problem:** Results are plain buttons rather than a listbox: no up and down arrows, no "No results" message, no result count and no scope. Choosing a result opens the chapter start without highlighting the term. Snippets are injected with `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` (escaped today, but fragile) in both `LibraryScreen.tsx` and `InBookSearchPanel.tsx`.

**Fix:** Use the listbox pattern with arrow keys and `aria-activedescendant`, a live-region count, a "No results for …" state and scope chips (Library, This collection, Notes). Highlight the term on arrival (see R1). Render snippets as React nodes from `{ before, match, after }` segments and remove both `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` uses.

**Done when:** Search can be driven entirely by keyboard and announces its result count to screen readers.

### L10 Duplicate and recovery dialogs

**Where:** `LibraryScreen.tsx`; `importService.ts`.

**Problem:** Importing 20 files with many duplicates asks 20 times, with no "apply to all". The duplicate dialog names only the incoming title. The recovery dialog closes after every single removal and has no "Remove all".

**Fix:** Add "Apply to all remaining" and show the existing item's title and date. Keep the recovery dialog open until the list is empty and add "Remove all".

**Done when:** A batch import with duplicates needs at most one decision.

### L11 Import pipeline limits and wrong error text

**Where:** `import/fileDetector.ts`, `lib/fileSource.ts`, `import/importService.ts`, `epubImporter.ts`.

**Problem:**

- `MAX_IMPORT_BYTES` is 50 MB, which many illustrated EPUBs exceed, and the message "This file is too large" gives no size or limit.
- `assertImportable` throws `COPY.drm` for any ".epub" that is not a zip (`COPY.drm ? COPY.drm : "Unreadable file"`), so a merely corrupt file says "This book is protected and can't be imported".
- `unzipSync` runs several times per import (validate, import, open) on the main thread, with no cap on uncompressed size or entry count (zip bomb).
- `pickImportFiles` and `filesFromTauriDrop` read all selected files into memory at once as number arrays.
- PDF is refused outright, and `.md` is treated as plain text.
- Progress is a single replaceable toast.

**Fix:** Raise the cap (about 200 MB, configurable) and say "This file is 63 MB; the limit is 50 MB". Correct the error copy to "This file isn't a valid EPUB". Stream files one at a time and decompress once. Cap uncompressed bytes and entry count. Show an import progress dialog with per-file status and Cancel. PDF support is a product decision flagged in F1.

**Done when:** A corrupt EPUB reports a corruption message, a zip bomb is rejected quickly, and a 15-file import shows per-file progress without freezing the window.

## 6. P1: Notes

### N1 The Notes screen is a flat list with no export

**Where:** `screens/NotesScreen.tsx`.

**Problem:** All annotations from all books are mixed in one list: no grouping by book, no search, sort, colour filter or date range. Rows do not show the chapter or date. The list is not virtualised. There is no export.

**Fix:** Group by book (collapsible, with counts). Add search across quotes and notes, sort (newest, oldest, book order) and colour chips, and show chapter plus date on every row. Add Export: Markdown (per book or all, with quote, note, chapter, date and location), CSV and "Copy all". Allow changing a highlight's colour from the row. Add a quote-card button.

**Done when:** A user can export one book's highlights to Markdown in two clicks.

### N2 Orphaned notes still open the reader

**Where:** `screens/NotesScreen.tsx`.

**Problem:** Notes whose book is gone show "\[missing document\]" but still open the reader, which errors.

**Fix:** Disable Open for missing documents, offer only Delete and Export, and add an explanatory line.

**Done when:** No row can navigate to a missing document.

## 7. P1/P2: Settings and About

### S1 Missing settings

**Where:** `SettingsScreen.tsx`; `onboarding/PreferencesEditor.tsx`; `reader/keepAwake.ts`.

**Problem:** Default reading preferences expose only theme, typeface and size (`savePrefs` writes just those three). The "keep screen awake while reading" preference (`preventSleepWhileReading` in the window-state file) is read by the reader but has no control. There is no UI scale, no shortcut reference and no automatic backup.

**Fix:** Add all default reading prefs (line spacing, margins, width, flow, spread); a keep-awake toggle; UI zoom (80 to 150%); default library sort and view; a backup folder with automatic rolling backups and a reminder; "Rebuild search index"; "Reset app data" behind a confirmation; and a Shortcuts section.

**Done when:** Every user-facing preference that the code reads can be changed in Settings.

### S2 Backup and restore: memory use and feedback

**Where:** `SettingsScreen.tsx` (`handleExport`, `handlePickRestore`, `loadStorage`); `backup/backupService.ts`; `backup/zipArchive.ts`.

**Problem:** The whole backup is built in memory and written with `invoke("fs_write_atomic", { data: Array.from(bytes) })`. Restore reads through `fs_read` into a number array. A library of several hundred MB will freeze the window or exhaust memory. Export has no progress or cancel. Library size is computed by calling `fs.stat` for each file one at a time. Result messages are plain paragraphs with no live region.

**Fix:** Do backup and restore in Rust with streaming (`backup_export(destPath)`, `backup_inspect(path)`) and emit progress events. Verify the finished archive by re-opening it and checking hashes. Add a `dir_size` command. Show messages as toasts (`role="status"`).

**Done when:** Exporting a 1 GB library keeps the UI responsive, shows progress, and the archive verifies.

### S3 About and legal

**Problem:** "Version" is the only About content. There are no licences or attributions (Readium, fflate, React, Zustand, bundled fonts) and no privacy statement.

**Fix:** An About card with version and build, a licences page, a plain privacy note ("nothing leaves your device"), a support link, "Copy diagnostics" and "Check for updates" (see E5).

**Done when:** Third-party notices ship inside the installer and are viewable in the app.

## 8. Shell, accessibility and internationalisation

### X1 Navigation and shell

**Where:** `shell/Shell.tsx`, `shell/Sidebar.tsx`, `store/routeStore.ts`, `main.tsx`.

**Problem:** The app always opens on Library even if you were mid-book. There is no back and forward history between screens and no command palette. The window title never changes from "Folio", and `core:window:allow-set-title` is not in the capability file. The sidebar is a fixed 232 px with no app identity and no shortcut hints (Ctrl+1 to 4 exist but are invisible), and it takes almost half the width at the 720 px minimum window.

**Fix:** An option "Reopen last book on launch" (persist last route, document and location). Alt+Left and Alt+Right history. Ctrl+K command palette (open book, run action, go to screen). Window title equals the current book. A collapsible sidebar below about 900 px. Shortcut hints in tooltips.

**Done when:** Relaunching resumes the last book when enabled, and the taskbar shows the book title.

### X2 Loading and empty states

**Where:** Library, Notes, Collections.

**Problem:** Loading is a plain "Loading…" line, and Notes shows it as a bare paragraph.

**Fix:** Skeleton rows for lists, with the shimmer disabled under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

### X3 Accessibility and contrast

**Where:** `tokens.css`, `components.css`, `reader.css`, `TocPanel.tsx`, `FolioChip.tsx`.

**Problem:**

- `--folio-text-muted` (`#87897F`) is 3.28:1 on the canvas and 3.11:1 on subtle surfaces in the light theme, below AA for text. Check every place it carries text.
- Light-theme `--folio-border` is 1.23:1 against the canvas (dark theme 1.61:1). Input and control boundaries should reach 3:1 (WCAG 1.4.11).
- There is no `forced-colors` or `prefers-contrast` support.
- Tabs in `TocPanel` use `role="tablist"` but lack Arrow-key roving focus.
- z-index values are ad hoc (10, 15, 19, 20, 30, 35, 40, 41, 45, 50, 60, 65, 70, 80, 90, 100).
- Modal detection relies on DOM queries (`hasBlockingOverlay`) instead of making the background `inert`.

**Fix:** Darken muted text to at least 4.5:1. Add a stronger `--folio-border-control` token for form controls. Add `@media (forced-colors: active)` rules and a high-contrast option. Add arrow-key roving to tabs and chips. Define a z-index scale in the tokens. Set `inert` on the app root while a modal is open.

**Done when:** axe (jest-axe or Playwright) reports no serious violations on Library, Reader, Notes and Settings in both themes, and a keyboard-only run-through completes every core flow.

### X4 Type scale and UI size

**Problem:** Micro text is 11 px and labels are 13 px, with no way to scale the app.

**Fix:** Raise the minimums to 12 and 14 px and add the UI zoom setting from S1.

### X5 Internationalisation (P2)

**Problem:** All UI strings are hard-coded English, although the importer detects Hindi content. Reading font stacks have no Devanagari-aware fallback and there is no right-to-left handling.

**Fix:** Extract strings into a catalogue (for example `t("library.title")`), add `Nirmala UI` to the font stacks, set `dir` and `lang` on content, and pass RTL page progression to the engine preferences.

## 9. Engineering and release

### E1 UI-thread blocking file I/O and number-array IPC (P1, performance)

**Where:** `src-tauri/src/commands/fs.rs`, `zip.rs`, `hash.rs`; `src/lib/fileStore.ts`, `fileSource.ts`; `SettingsScreen.tsx`; `backup/zipArchive.ts`.

**Problem:** Every command is a synchronous `#[tauri::command] pub fn`, which Tauri runs on the main thread, including the `thread::sleep` retry loops in rename. Bytes travel as `Vec<u8>`, which serialises to a JSON array of numbers; the TypeScript side does `Array.from(data)` and `new Uint8Array(arr)`. A 50 MB EPUB becomes a payload several times larger than the file. Importing, opening, covers and backups therefore freeze the window.

**Fix:** Make commands `async` (or `#[tauri::command(async)]`) and use `spawn_blocking` for disk work. Return file bytes as `tauri::ipc::Response` and accept raw request bodies for writes (`invoke(cmd, bytes, { headers })`). Add `dir_size`, streaming backup and a `read_many` for small files such as covers and meta. Use unique temp file names in `fs_write_atomic`.

**Done when:** Importing a 50 MB EPUB keeps the UI responsive (frame time under 50 ms) and peak memory stays within about twice the file size. `scripts/perf.ts` runs in CI against a budget.

### E2 Reader code structure and hook hygiene

**Where:** `ReaderScreen.tsx` (1,487 lines, 5 `eslint-disable` comments); `package.json` (no ESLint).

**Problem:** One component owns the engine lifecycle, annotations, keyboard, chrome, panels, search and dialogs. The engine effect closes over `isFocusMode` without listing it, so it is stale in the click and pointer callbacks. It also depends on `request` identity, so a new request object rebuilds the whole engine. ESLint is not configured, so the `eslint-disable` comments protect nothing.

**Fix:** Split into `useReaderEngine`, `useAnnotations`, `useReaderKeyboard`, `useReaderChrome` and `useInBookSearch`, each testable. Add ESLint with `react-hooks`, `jsx-a11y` and `@typescript-eslint`, plus Prettier. Fix stale closures with refs. Make the engine effect depend on `docId` and `retryNonce` only, and navigate rather than rebuild when the location changes.

**Done when:** Lint passes with no `eslint-disable` for exhaustive-deps, and toggling focus mode behaves identically on first and later toggles.

### E3 Tauri capabilities and window features \[verify in a release build\]

**Where:** `src-tauri/capabilities/default.json`; `src/lib/fullscreen.ts`; `src/lib/appWindow.ts`.

**Problem:** Only `core:default`, `allow-destroy`, `allow-show`, `opener:default` and `dialog:default` are granted. `fullscreen.ts` calls `setFullscreen`, which is not part of the default window permissions, so F11 may be rejected in a production build, and the call is fire-and-forget so the failure would be silent. Setting the window title needs `core:window:allow-set-title`.

**Fix:** Add the specific window permissions that are used (set-fullscreen, set-title) and nothing broader. Handle rejection with a toast.

**Done when:** F11 and the dynamic window title work in an installed release build.

### E4 Tests and CI

**Problem:** The README cites 107 Vitest and 28 Rust tests, but there are no end-to-end or accessibility tests, and the CI workflow was not provided.

**Fix:** Add Playwright (or Tauri WebDriver) smoke tests: first run, import an EPUB, open it, highlight, close, reopen and check it resumes on the same page; backup export then restore. Add jest-axe checks. CI matrix: `tsc -b`, ESLint, Vitest, `cargo test`, `cargo clippy -D warnings`, `cargo audit`, `pnpm audit`, installer build, and `scripts/perf.ts` against budgets.

**Done when:** A pull request cannot merge with a failing smoke, accessibility or performance check.

### E5 Release and distribution

**Where:** `tauri.conf.json`, `Cargo.toml`, `README.md`, `.env.example`.

**Problem:** NSIS only. No code-signing configuration, so Windows SmartScreen will warn. No updater plugin. No in-app way to report a crash other than finding the log file. `icon.icns` is listed but macOS and Linux are not built, and `jumplist.rs` is Windows-only. `README.md` still carries a historical phase log and Drive-sync and dictionary instructions, and `.env.example` still documents `VITE_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` for a removed feature. The README links to `../docs/…` files that are not in this repo.

**Fix:** Sign the installer (Authenticode or Azure Trusted Signing). Add `tauri-plugin-updater` with signed manifests and a user-initiated "Check for updates" (no background telemetry). Decide the platform matrix and state it in the README. Rewrite the README (install, dev, test, release, architecture, data layout). Delete the stale env vars and the Drive and dictionary sections. Add a LICENSE and third-party notices. Add "Copy diagnostics" in Settings.

**Done when:** A signed installer installs without a SmartScreen warning, updates work end to end, and a new contributor can build from the README alone.

### E6 Rust startup robustness

**Where:** `src-tauri/src/lib.rs`.

**Problem:** `let _ = std::fs::create_dir_all(...)` ignores failure. If the app directory cannot be created (permissions, roaming profile), the app starts and every later operation fails with obscure errors.

**Fix:** Check the result and show a blocking, plain-language error dialog with the path and a "Choose another folder" option.

**Done when:** A read-only app directory produces a clear message on launch.

### E7 Minor correctness items

- `ReadingSessionDialog` receives `Date.now() - sessionStartTsRef.current` computed at render, so the session duration does not tick while the dialog is open.
- `getLibraryManager()` builds a new manager per call, and each screen re-reads manifest, meta and annotations from disk. Add a small cache with change events (P2).
- The `FolioDialog` Close button position is set with inline styles. Move it to CSS.
- Theme and sort preference live in `localStorage`, which is not in the backup. Include them (additive settings file).
- Settings messages and theme chips use inline styles (`marginRight: 8`). Move to CSS classes.

## 10. Roadmap

**Phase 1 (first week): stabilise.** P0-1 to P0-5, R7, the contrast tokens in X3, L6, E3.

**Phase 2: reader experience.** R1 to R6, R8 to R14, R16, with the E2 refactor done alongside so the new behaviour lands in testable hooks.

**Phase 3: performance and library.** E1, L1 to L3, S2, R12, then L4 to L11 and N1 to N2.

**Phase 4: polish and release.** S1 to S3, X1 to X5, E4 to E7.

**Phase 5: features.** Section 11 items in product-priority order.

## 11. Feature backlog

- **F1 PDF support** (pdf.js), Markdown rendering and CBZ. P2, needs a product decision: PDF is refused today by design.
- **F2 Reading stats:** per-book total time, daily time, streaks and goals from `pace.sessionsMs`; an "Insights" view. P2.
- **F3 Text-to-speech** using the Web Speech API, with follow-along highlighting and speed control. P2.
- **F4 Annotation export** to Obsidian and Notion-friendly Markdown (see N1). P1.
- **F5 Add from URL or clipboard**, reusing `clip/epubBuilder.ts` (an EPUB builder exists with no UI). P2; needs explicit consent for network use.
- **F6 Lookup on select** (dictionary or translate): removed by decision. If revisited, make it opt-in with a clear privacy note. P3, product decision.
- **F7 Folder import** and watch-folder auto-import. P2.
- **F8 Authors, series and tag views**, with metadata editing (L4). P2.
- **F9 Reader extras:** two-page spread control (R15), page-turn animation toggle, line-focus ruler, margins by characters, per-book language and hyphenation. P2 and P3.
- **F10 Multiple windows** to read two books side by side. P3.
- **F11 Backup to a chosen folder** with rolling copies and reminders, as the user-controlled replacement for the removed cloud sync (for example a OneDrive or Dropbox folder). P1 and P2.

## 12. Manual QA checklist before release

1. Fresh install in light and dark: every button label is readable, onboarding completes, the tour completes.
2. Import a 5 MB, a 60 MB and a corrupt EPUB, a DRM EPUB, a PDF, an HTML and a TXT file; each gives a correct message.
3. Drag 20 files onto the window, including duplicates; the window stays responsive and the result summary is accurate.
4. Open a book, turn pages, close and reopen: the position resumes. Kill the process mid-read: at most a few seconds of progress are lost.
5. Search for a word that appears many times; step through matches with the panel still open; the term is highlighted.
6. Highlight, change colour, add a note, delete and undo; check on all four reader themes.
7. Open Appearance and change size, margins and spread while watching the page without a scrim.
8. Keyboard only: complete import, open, search, bookmark, notes export and settings without a mouse; check focus never jumps.
9. Screen reader pass (NVDA) over Library, Reader chrome, dialogs and toasts.
10. Switch the OS between light and dark with reading theme set to System.
11. Export a backup, wipe the library, restore (merge and replace) and verify notes, progress and collections.
12. Install on a clean Windows 10 and 11 machine: file association, single instance, jump list, F11, window title, updater.
13. Throw a test error in each screen: the recovery screen appears and the log file records it.

## 13. What to preserve

These parts are already strong. Do not regress them while fixing the items above.

- Write ordering and atomic writes: data files first, manifest last, per-path mutex, recovery detection for interrupted imports and restores.
- The `ReaderNavigationCoordinator` (serialised moves, coalesced destinations, superseded-outcome handling) and the progress write gates.
- The modal stack and focus trap approach, and `inert` on hidden reader chrome.
- Privacy posture: local-only diagnostics, no telemetry, an HTML sanitizer that drops scripts and forms, and a strict CSP.
- Reduced-motion handling, `aria-keyshortcuts` and tooltips on reader controls, and the deterministic EPUB builder.
- The shared component library (`Folio*`), which keeps screens visually consistent.

# Folio Desktop — Production-Readiness Plan (Phases 1–4)

Source: the 12 Nov 2026 production-readiness report. Scope: full roadmap,
Phases 1–4 (stabilise → reader → performance/library → polish & release).
Feature backlog (§11, Phase 5) is out of scope except where absorbed by a
P-item (e.g. F4 export → N1).

## Working rules

1. **Verify-then-fix.** The report was written from an older snapshot. Before
   touching any item, re-check the current tree; items already fixed by
   S-20261107/08/09 work (toast host, delete confirmation, index caching,
   snippet escaping, panel contrast) get a regression test or are closed with
   evidence, never a duplicate fix.
2. **Frozen invariants** (from AGENTS.md / report §1, §13):
   - Schema-1 field names/enum strings in `desktop/src/model/types.ts` are
     additive-only; preserve unknown keys.
   - Manifest-last write ordering, per-path mutex in `fileStore.ts` /
     `libraryManager.ts`; coordinator-driven navigation.
   - No network calls, no telemetry; CSP stays strict; no revival of Drive
     sync (D-20261031-03) or the dictionary (D-20261031-05).
   - Token changes update `tests/fixtures/tokens.json` in the same commit.
3. **Verification on this Linux host:** `tsc -b`, Vitest, `vite build`,
   `cargo check --all-targets --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu` (cross-check)
   and Linux-runnable `cargo test`. Windows-only behaviours (installer,
   junctions at runtime, F11/title permissions, webview feel) are coded +
   unit-tested where possible and recorded as Windows-verification-pending in
   `docs/development/TASKS.md`, matching existing conventions.
4. **Git:** work on the current tree. No commits/pushes without explicit
   authorization.
5. **Bookkeeping:** each phase updates `docs/development/TASKS.md` (new FT-0xx
   rows) and `docs/development/CURRENT_SESSION.md` at milestones; stable IDs
   (`S-`/`R-`) for any audit records created.

---

## Phase 1 — Stabilise (P0 blockers + quick wins)

Order chosen so later phases build on it: error handling (P0-4) first, since
every other phase's fixes need a way to report failures.

### Step 1.1 — P0-4: error logging + `handleError`
- Files: `desktop/src/lib/errorLog.ts`, `ReaderScreen.tsx`,
  `LibraryScreen.tsx`, `SettingsScreen.tsx`, `libraryUi.ts`, `NotesScreen.tsx`.
- Add `handleError(error, { context, userMessage?, toast? })` that always
  calls `reportError` and optionally raises the existing global toast.
- Sweep every `catch` block: deliberate silence (still logged) vs toast.
  Wrap unprotected awaits in `ReaderScreen.tsx` (`createAnnotation`,
  `saveNote`, `toggleHighlight`, TocPanel callbacks) with try/catch + toast,
  keeping dialogs open with draft intact (pattern from
  `NotesScreen.handleEditSave`).
- Done when: forcing rejection on each call shows a toast, writes one log
  line, UI stays usable. Unit test per call-site class.

### Step 1.2 — P0-1: dark-theme contrast tokens
- Files: `tokens.css`, `components.css`, `tests/fixtures/tokens.json`,
  reuse `src/lib/contrast.ts`.
- Add dark overrides: `--folio-on-accent` (dark green, e.g. `#14201A`),
  `--folio-danger-container` (dark red-brown), `--folio-on-danger-container`
  (light pink). Check `.folio-btn--solid-danger` in both themes.
- Test: parse both token blocks; assert ≥4.5:1 text pairs and ≥3:1 borders /
  focus rings, light + dark; keep tokens.json pinned equality.

### Step 1.3 — P0-2: focus-steal in FolioPanel / FolioDialog
- Files: `FolioPanel.tsx`, `FolioDialog.tsx`, callers in `ReaderScreen.tsx`.
- `onClose` into a ref updated each render; effect deps `[open]` only; restore
  focus only on actual close; add `data-autofocus` to search input, note
  textarea, other primary fields.
- Done when: parent re-render with new `onClose` does not move focus; typing
  multi-char in-book search keeps focus in input.

### Step 1.4 — P0-3: error boundaries
- Files: new `src/shell/ErrorBoundary.tsx`; wire in `main.tsx` (root) and
  around `ReaderScreen`.

### Step 1.5 — P0-5: Rust command sandbox
- Files: `guard.rs`, `commands/fs.rs`, `commands/zip.rs`, `commands/hash.rs`,

- Canonicalise every path; require containment in app data dir after
  symlink/junction resolution. Allow outside paths only from native
  dialog/drop/launch-argument events registered this session (Tauri managed
  state allow-list). Cap `zip_read` by entry count and total uncompressed
  bytes (zip bombs). Drop the dead `ensure_no_escape` or use it properly.
- Done when (Linux-runnable): Rust unit tests reject `/folio-library/../x`
  and non-app-root absolutes; junction case unit-tested with cfg(windows) +

### Step 1.6 — Quick wins
- **R7** icons: add Copy, Image/Share, EyeOff, Pencil to `FolioIcons.tsx`;

- **X3 (token slice)**: darken `--folio-text-muted` to ≥4.5:1; add

### Step 2.0 — E2: reader refactor
- Split `ReaderScreen.tsx` (1,487 lines) into `useReaderEngine`,
  `useAnnotations`, `useReaderKeyboard`, `useReaderChrome`, `useInBookSearch`.

- Done when: lint passes clean; focus-mode toggle behaves identically on

### Step 2.1 — R1+R2+R3: search quality
- Shared `htmlToText()` (entity decode, block→space, skip
  script/style/head); single utility for search, positions, importers,
  library index. Fixture with `&`, ` `, `’`.
- Per-occurrence in-book search: all matches per chapter (phrase first,
  then all-words), text-anchored locator (quote ±32 chars) so `goAnchored`
  lands on the match; group by chapter with counts; panel stays open; Next/
  Prev (Enter/Shift+Enter/F3); "3 of 41" counter; temporary decoration group
  for the active match, cleared on close; 2-char minimum enforced.
- MiniSearch: adopt the real `minisearch` package or add cached DFs,
  precomputed TFs, sorted vocab + binary-search prefixes, offset map for
  correct accent/fuzzy/prefix highlights, quoted phrase support; index in a
  Web Worker; library indexing with progress.
- Done when: 30 occurrences in one chapter → 30 navigable, highlighted
  results; 3 MB book <100 ms after index; accents/fuzzy/prefix highlight.

### Step 2.2 — R4: back navigation
- Route internal links through the navigation coordinator (fix
  `handleLocator` calling `navigator.go` directly); position-history stack on
  every absolute move/link follow; "Back to where you were" snackbar action
  (Phase 2 uses existing toasts until R14 unifies them); Alt+Left binding.
- Footnote popover for `epub:type="noteref"` instead of navigation.

### Step 2.3 — R5: interactive highlights
- Subscribe to decoration activation; popover at highlight: change colour,
  add/edit note, copy, delete with Undo toast. Overlapping selection updates
  the existing annotation (no duplicates); toolbar shows active colour.
- Done when: click opens popover; colour change updates in place; no
  overlapping duplicates; delete undoable.

### Step 2.4 — R14: unify notifications
- Remove `navNotice`/reader snackbar; global host everywhere; stack ≤3,
  per-tone styling, action buttons (Undo/Back), pause on hover/focus,
  collision-safe keys. Needed before R5's Undo ships.
- Done when: error toast never replaced by success; Undo works from toast.

### Step 2.5 — R8: single active panel
- `activePanel` state (`"toc" | "appearance" | "search" | null`);

### Step 2.6 — R13: keyboard model
- Ignore letter shortcuts with modifiers; move modal Escape into

- **R9**: pass resolved `systemDark` into `applyPrefs`; re-submit prefs on OS
  change; OS theme switch repaints the open book.
- **R6**: Share acts on live selection via selection toolbar;

  "Copy with citation".
- **R11**: finer slider steps (0.1%) + chapter ticks + scrub tooltip;
  "1 h 25 min left"; per-chapter time; floor percent labels; Finished state
  + end-of-book card.
- **R12**: async/streaming unzip (fflate async or Worker), lazy resource
  decompression, lazy/cached position generation, progress-aware splash
  timer replacing the 8 s failsafe.
- **R16**: one highlight-palette module, theme-aware (translucent/darker
  tints on dark reader themes); ≥4.5:1 on all four reader themes; token
  fixture updated if swatch tokens change.

---

## Phase 3 — Performance and library

### Step 3.1 — E1: async IPC + streaming bytes
- Make Tauri commands `async` + `spawn_blocking`; return bytes via
  `tauri::ipc::Response`, accept raw request bodies for writes; unique temp
  names in `fs_write_atomic`; add `dir_size`, `read_many`; streaming backup
  groundwork for S2.
- Done when (Linux measurable): `scripts/perf.ts` budgets pass; unit tests
  for new commands; runtime frame-time check deferred to Windows.

### Step 3.2 — R12 support: import/open decompression once
- `epubPublication.ts`: decompress once, lazy resources, position cache

  size-stating message; fix DRM error copy for corrupt files; stream files
  one at a time; entry-count + uncompressed-size caps; per-file progress
  dialog with Cancel.

### Step 3.3 — L1+L2+L3: library list performance
- Keep list on refresh (loading only when empty; subtle progress bar
  otherwise); bounded parallelism (~8) + meta cache by `updatedAt`;
  incremental row update after import.
- Thumbnails at import (additive file), IntersectionObserver lazy covers,
  virtualised list/grid.
- Default sort "Recent activity" (later of last-read and imported-at); add

  sensitivity: "base" })`; highlight + scroll to newly imported row.

### Step 3.4 — S2: Rust streaming backup

25: ## Stack and runtimes
26: 
27: - **Frontend:** React 18.3, TypeScript 5.6 (strict, `noUnusedLocals`,
28:   `noUnusedParameters`, `noFallthroughCasesInSwitch`), Vite 5, Zustand 4.
29: - **Reader:** Readium web toolkit (`@readium/navigator`, `@readium/shared`).
30: - **Shell:** Tauri 2, Rust 2021 edition, NSIS installer for Windows.
31: - **Tests:** Vitest 2 with `jsdom`; no snapshot suites.
32: - **Data:** plain JSON files through a `FileStore` port; no app database.
33: - **CI:** pnpm 11, Node 22, `windows-latest`.

35: ## Commands
36: 
37: Run from `desktop/` unless noted.
38: 
39: ```bash
40: pnpm install                  # CI uses --frozen-lockfile
41: pnpm exec tsc -b              # typecheck (strict)
42: pnpm exec vitest run          # all unit tests
43: pnpm exec vitest run tests/reader.test.ts
44: pnpm exec vitest run tests/reader.test.ts -t "progress"
45: pnpm exec vite build          # frontend production build
46: pnpm tauri:dev                # requires a working desktop webview
47: pnpm tauri:build              # NSIS installer
48: cd src-tauri
49: cargo test --all-targets
50: cargo fmt --all -- --check
51: ```
52: 
53: The CI order is: `tsc -b` → `vitest run` → `vite build` → `cargo test` →
54: `cargo fmt --check` → `tauri build` (artifact upload).

56: If `pnpm` is not installed (it is absent in this Linux VM) but `node_modules`
57: exists, use `./node_modules/.bin/tsc -b`, `./node_modules/.bin/vitest run`, and
58: `./node_modules/.bin/vite build` from `desktop/`.

60: ## Environment constraints
61: 
62: - **Full builds are Windows-only.** Linux lacks `webkit2gtk`/`gtk3`. `cargo test` and
63:   `pnpm tauri:*` are not valid Linux verification here. Do not claim they
64:   passed. (The sync-only `keyring`/`reqwest` crates were removed with Drive
65:   sync, 2026-10-31 — see D-20261031-03.)
66: - Linux-safe verification: `tsc -b`, Vitest, `vite build`.
67: - Vite dev server uses fixed port `1420` (`strictPort`). It ignores
68:   `**/src-tauri/**` while watching because cargo's locked debug DLL crashed the
69:   watcher with `EBUSY` on Windows.
70: - Google Drive sync was removed (2026-10-31, D-20261031-03); the app makes no
71:   network requests. Do not reintroduce network hosts into the CSP.
72: - The offline dictionary was removed entirely (2026-10-31, D-20261031-05);
73:   `tests/noDictionary.test.ts` guards against re-introducing it.
74: - **COM string values must use task memory.** A `VT_LPWSTR` in a
75:   `PROPVARIANT` (for example `PKEY_Title` on a jump-list `IShellLink`) is
76:   freed by the shell with `CoTaskMemFree`. Backing it with a Rust `Vec` buffer
77:   corrupted the process heap and killed the app at startup
78:   (`0xC0000374`) — see
79:   [`A-BUG-20261031-01`](audits/bugs/A-BUG-20261031-01-jumplist-startup-crash.md).
80:   Allocate with `CoTaskMemAlloc` and release with `PropVariantClear`.
81: 
82: ## Architecture
83: 
84: **Frontend owns the application model.** Screens, importers, reader behavior,
85: search, annotations, backup/merge logic are TypeScript. Rust is a thin,
86: generic OS bridge and must not parse `DocMeta`/`Manifest` or hardcode Folio
87: layout.
88: 
89: **Rust commands** (`desktop/src-tauri/src/lib.rs`):
90: `fs_read`, `fs_write_atomic`, `fs_delete`, `fs_move`, `fs_stat`, `fs_list_dir`,
91: `fs_free_space`, `sha256_file`, `zip_read`, `zip_write`, `open_external_url`,
92: `open_app_dir`, `library_path`, `prevent_display_sleep`, and
93: `take_pending_launch`. (The OAuth signIn/refresh/status/sign-out commands were
94: removed with Drive sync, 2026-10-31; the `dict_*` commands with the
95: dictionary removal, D-20261031-05.)
96: 
97: **Virtual paths.** TypeScript builds all library paths under `/folio-library`
98: (`desktop/src/lib/libraryPaths.ts`). Rust translates that prefix to the real app
99: dir in `desktop/src-tauri/src/appdir.rs`; native/UNC paths pass through. Every
100: Rust write goes through `guard.rs` (absolute-path + traversal checks).
101: 
102: **On-disk layout.** Default app dir is `%APPDATA%/Folio` (Windows); the library
103: root is `<appDir>/library`:
104: 
105: ```
106: library/manifest.json                 # commit point
107: library/docs/<slug>/                  # meta.json, original/, clean/, reading/, cover
108: library/user/{annotations,progress,collections,settings,doc-settings}.json
109: library/index/text/<docId>.json       # device-local search cache
110: <appDir>/user/window.json             # desktop-only window geometry
111: ```
112: 
113: (Sync had an `<appDir>/sync/state.json`; it is read/written by nothing since
114: the 2026-10-31 removal and can be deleted manually.)
115: 
116: **Import pipeline** (`src/import/`): format detection/refusals (PDF, DRM,
117: rights, 50 MB cap) → HTML sanitizer → TXT/HTML/EPUB import → deterministic
118: `EpubBuilder` → dedup gate (Skip / Keep both / Replace) → `LibraryManager`
119: commit → recovery detection for damaged docs/interrupted imports.
120: 
121: **Reader** (`src/reader/`): Readium navigator adapter, positions, TOC/cover
122: parsing, themes/typography, progress with write gates, resume cascade, pace,
123: chrome state, keep-awake. Reader route is `src/screens/ReaderScreen.tsx`.
124: (Drive sync was removed 2026-10-31 — see D-20261031-03.)
125: 
126: ## Data-model invariants (highest risk)
127: 
128: Source of truth: `.docs/05-data-model-and-compat.md` and
129: `desktop/src/model/types.ts`.
130: 
131: - Schema-1 JSON field names, optionality, and enum strings are frozen for
132:   compatibility with the Android app.
133: - Unknown keys must survive read → patch → rewrite.
134: - `manifest.json` is written **last** after any doc mutation.
135: - `collections.json` `docIds` ↔ `docMeta.collectionIds` are dual-written through
136:   shared mutators.
137: - Doc deletion cascades: folder → index → annotations/progress/collections/
138:   doc-settings → manifest last.
139: - Content hash is SHA-256 hex. Slugs are lowercase-with-dashes with `-2`
140:   collision suffixes.
141: - Backup ZIP contract is defined in `.docs/05` §5; the Drive mirror contract
142:   (§6) is retired with the feature removal (2026-10-31, D-20261031-03).
143:

146: - `tests/fixtures/*.json` are compact, byte-identical round-trip fixtures.

154: - There is no integration/E2E suite and no required external service for the

- Work through the 12 Nov 2026 Folio Desktop production-readiness report (a large P0/P1/P2 audit) following the plan phases 1–4: stabilise → reader → performance/library → polish & release. Currently in Phase 1 (P0 blockers + quick wins).

## Requirements
- Work on current tree directly; nothing committed/pushed without explicit authorization (user approved this and chose "Full roadmap (Phases 1–4)" scope).
- Plan file written at `/home/heheharshprajapati/.opencode/plan/folio-production-readiness.md` (detailed item-by-item plan with IDs, done-when criteria).
- Frozen invariants: schema-1 additive-only, manifest-last writes, no network/telemetry, token changes must update `tests/fixtures/tokens.json` in same commit, keep coordinator/modal-stack/mutex patterns.
- Linux host: verify via `tsc -b`, Vitest, `vite build`, `cargo test -p foliocore`; Windows-only runtime items recorded as blocked, never claimed as passing.

## Decisions
- Verify-then-fix per item: report was written from older snapshot; some items already done by prior sessions (toast host, delete confirmation, snippet escaping, panel contrast, index caching).
- Kept existing decision A-UI-20261031-03 (muted text stays decorative below AA; functional labels use `--folio-text-secondary`) instead of blanket-darkening `--folio-text-muted`.
- Expected-control-flow catches (e.g. "no index yet" per book) left silent; genuine failures logged via new `handleError`.
- Rust security core split into new dependency-free sub-crate `src-tauri/foliocore/` (appdir.rs, guard.rs, sandbox.rs) so tests run on Linux; main crate re-exports `pub use foliocore::{appdir, guard, sandbox}`.
- Zip crate trimmed to `{ version = "2", default-features = false, features = ["deflate"] }` (removed C-codec cross-compile blocker; backup zips handled in TS anyway).
- Sandbox design: paths inside app dir allowed; outside paths only if granted this session (exact-path grants only, no parent-dir grants); grants made Rust-side via new dialog commands (`pick_import_files`, `pick_backup_source`, `pick_backup_dest`, `pick_image_dest`) and window DragDrop Drop event (`folio://drop-granted` emitted after grant); launch args granted in `open_files::remember`.
- Frontend dialog/drop flows must be rewired to the new Rust commands + `folio://drop-granted` event (NOT YET DONE).

## Work State
### Completed
- **P0-4**: `handleError(error, {context, userMessage?, details?})` + `describeError()` added to `desktop/src/lib/errorLog.ts`; tests in `tests/errorLog.test.ts` (8 passing). Swept user-facing catches in ReaderScreen (createAnnotation/toggleHighlight/saveNote/handleCopySelection/handleBookmarkToggle/TocPanel callbacks — dialogs stay open with drafts on failure), NotesScreen, CollectionsScreen, LibraryScreen, SettingsScreen, libraryUi.ts, TocPanel, InBookSearchPanel, QuoteCard.
- **P0-1**: dark tokens added (`--folio-on-accent: #14201A`, `--folio-danger-container: #3A2220`, `--folio-on-danger-container: #F3C9C4`), plus additive `--folio-border-control` (light `#8A897C`, dark `#748074`) in tokens.css + fixture updated; border-control wired into `.folio-searchbar__input`, `.folio-filter-select`, `.folio-note-input`, `.folio-inbook-search-panel__field`; contrast.test.ts extended (button/snackbar AA pairs + border 3:1 test); all token/contrast tests pass.
- **P0-2**: FolioPanel/FolioDialog use `onCloseRef` pattern, effect deps `[open]` only; `data-autofocus` added to in-book search input, both note textareas; new `tests/focusStability.test.tsx` (5 tests, passing).
- **P0-3**: `desktop/src/shell/ErrorBoundary.tsx` (root + reader variants, reload/log-folder/copy-diagnostics/back-to-library); wired in App.tsx (root) and Shell.tsx (around ReaderScreen with `onRecover={() => setRoute("library")}`); `.folio-errorboundary*` CSS classes in components.css; tests/errorBoundary.test.tsx (5 passing).
- **P0-5 (Rust, partially)**: foliocore sub-crate created; `guard_sandboxed()` implemented (canonicalize deepest existing ancestor, reject outside app dir unless granted); sandbox.rs grant/is_granted; zip.rs rewritten with zip-bomb caps (MAX_ENTRIES 20k, 4 GiB total, 2 GiB/entry, bounded read loop) + sandbox guard; fs/hash commands use `guard_sandboxed`; `commands/pick.rs` written; lib.rs registers sandbox module, pick commands, DragDrop Drop grant + emit; open_files::remember grants launch paths; new tests in guard/sandbox/zip/fs (incl. `rejects_paths_outside_the_sandbox` proving fs_delete can't remove outside paths).

Effects are intended to synchronize state between React and external systems such as manually updating the DOM, state management libraries, or other platform APIs. In general, the body of an effect should do one or both of the following:
* Update external systems with the latest state from React.
* Subscribe for updates from some external system, calling setState in a callback function when external state changes.

Calling setState synchronously within an effect body causes cascading renders that can hurt performance, and is not recommended. (https://react.dev/learn/you-might-not-need-an-effect).
