# Folio Desktop — Search Architecture Report

## 1. Library search — `desktop/src/search/miniSearch.ts` & `normalise.ts`

### `src/search/miniSearch.ts` (201 lines)
A hand-rolled BM25-ish index — **not the `minisearch` npm package** (comment at L1–4: port of mobile `MiniSearch.kt` semantics, k1=1.2, b=0.7, fuzzy 0.2, prefix matching, AND).

**Exports:**
- `interface SearchDoc` (L7–18): `{ id, title, text, docId?, docTitle?, href?, chapterTitle? }`
- `interface SearchHit` (L20–29): `{ id, score, snippet, docId?, docTitle?, href?, chapterTitle? }`
- `escapeHtml(value)` (L32–39): escapes `& < > " '` — used because `snippet` embeds `<mark>` and is rendered via `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`.
- `class MiniSearch` (L72–199), default export L201.

**Index build:** `add(doc)` (L78–86) tokenizes `title + " " + text` once and stores an inverted index `Map<term, Set<docIndex>>`. Tokenization (L45–52) = `normalizeQuery` then split on `[^a-z0-9\u0900-\u097f]+` (latin + Devanagari).

**Matching:** `termMatches` (L117–126) = exact, prefix, or fuzzy (query & term >4 chars; edit distance ≤1, ≤2 if len ≥8). `candidateIndices` (L92–115) = AND-intersection across tokens, scanning **every inverted-index term** per token (O(terms) per query token). Scoring (L150–167) is BM25 with `AVG_LEN = 200` fixed plus a +0.5 title boost per matched token.

**Snippets / highlighting offsets:** `snippet()` (L177–198) — *there are no byte offsets returned*; it finds the first case-insensitive `indexOf` of any query token in the raw text, slices ±40 chars around it, escapes everything, and wraps the matched slice in `<mark>…</mark>`. If no raw-text occurrence is found (e.g. fuzzy/prefix-only match, or the match is in the title), it returns the first 120 escaped chars with **no mark**. Original casing preserved inside `<mark>`.

### `src/search/normalise.ts` (69 lines)
- `normalizeQuery` (L5–18), also exported as `normalize` and default (L68–69). Order is load-bearing (spec 06 §6): **NFC → lowercase → strip ZWJ/ZWNJ (`\u200C\u200D`) → latin-only accent folding → collapse whitespace**. Devanagari combining marks deliberately preserved.
- `LATIN_FOLD` table (L20–58), `foldLatinAccents` (L60–66).

### Callers of miniSearch/normalise (complete grep)
| File | Lines | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `src/screens/LibraryScreen.tsx` | L11, 58–136 | Library full-text search UI (see §4) |
| `src/reader/readiumEngine.ts` | L28, 47–48, 248–298 | In-book search index (see §2) |

Note: `normalizeQuery` is only consumed inside `miniSearch.ts` itself; nothing else imports `normalise` directly.

### Caching
- Library: `searchIndexRef` in LibraryScreen keyed by `searchSignature(rows)` from `src/lib/searchCache.ts` (whole file, 8 lines: `rows.map(r => `${id}\0${title}`).join("\u0001")`) + a `searchIndexVersion` bump (L103) so queries typed mid-build re-run. Debounce 250 ms (L130–136). Index is rebuilt by **reading every book's `index/text/<docId>.json` from disk** (L62–104).
- Reader engine: `searchIndex`/`searchIndexPromise` (readiumEngine.ts L47–48) — lazy, cached for the life of the book; on failure the cached promise is dropped so the next query retries (L277–283).

## 2. In-book search

### `src/screens/reader/useInBookSearch.ts` (101 lines)
State hook owning panel open/query/results. `useInBookSearch({ engineRef })` (L19). Debounced effect (L29–65): 250 ms, sequence-token guard (`inbookSearchSeqRef`) against stale results, calls **`engine.search(query)`** (L49) — the `ReaderEngine` interface method, not Readium's own search API. `InBookSearchHit = { chapterTitle, snippetHtml, locator }` (L8–12). Exposes `toggle` (Ctrl+F), `clear` (keeps panel open), `reset` (doc change → closes panel).

### `src/components/InBookSearchPanel.tsx` (180 lines)
- Count bar: `"1 match found"` / `N matches found` (L113). Status hint "Enter at least 2 characters…" (L117) — but **the hook does not actually enforce a 2-char minimum**; `engine.search` only checks `query.trim()`.
- Results rendered with `dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: hit.snippetHtml }}` (L164) — the snippet's `<mark>` markup is why `escapeHtml` exists.
- Click handling (L43–66): per-locator `resolvingLocator` state, disables all cards while navigating; on failure shows "Couldn't reach that search location."; **on success the panel closes** (`onClose()` L58). So the panel does NOT stay open after navigating to a hit.
- Wired in `src/screens/ReaderScreen.tsx` L743–755; `onSelectResult` calls `goToHref(loc, "search")` (L752–754) → `navRef.goToHref(href, "search")` → `engine.go(href)`. **The locator is just the chapter href — no fragment, no text anchor** — so a result jump lands at the chapter start, not at the match. No decorations are applied to search hits.

### The engine's search — `src/reader/readiumEngine.ts`
- `search(query)` (L288–298): builds/gets the cached MiniSearch, `idx.search(query, 50)` (limit 50), maps hits to `{ chapterTitle, snippetHtml: h.snippet, locator: h.href ?? h.id }`.
- `getSearchIndex()` (L248–286): lazily dynamic-imports MiniSearch, iterates `pub.readingOrder.items`, reads each resource via `pub.get(link).read()` (Readium Publication API), and converts HTML→text with a local regex `stripHtml` (L570–577: removes `<script>/<style>`, then `<[^>]+>`, collapses whitespace — **no entity decoding**). No use of Readium's built-in search navigator; no Web Worker; runs synchronously on the main thread.

**No navigator-level search APIs are used anywhere** — the Readium `search`/`SearchNavigator` module is absent; both searches are MiniSearch-over-extracted-text.

## 3. Text extraction (HTML→text)

Four independent implementations:

1. **`src/reader/readiumEngine.ts` L570–577 `stripHtml`** — regex strip of script/style/tags + whitespace collapse, **no entity decoding** (so `&` stays literal in the in-book search corpus).
2. **`src/reader/positions.ts`** — `decodeEntities` (L22–36): supports a tiny named set (`amp lt gt quot apos nbsp #39`) plus numeric hex/dec refs. `textLengthOfHtml` (L41–56): regex strip (incl. `<?xml?>`, comments, script/style/head) → decode entities → whitespace collapse → **length only**, for the positions list (`POSITION_LENGTH = 1024`, L10). `generatePositions` (L72–104) builds one locator per ~1024 chars.
3. **`src/import/sanitize.ts`** — DOM-based: `textFromHtml` (L181–188) parses with `DOMParser`, removes script/style, uses `body.textContent` + whitespace normalization. `paragraphsFromHtml` (L201–209) takes `p, li, h1..h6, blockquote` `textContent`. Used for article import and (via `textFromHtml`) for EPUB import chapter text.
4. **`src/import/epubImporter.ts` L98–123 `parseEpub`** — for each spine item, `DOMParser` for heading (h1–h3/title, L108–112) and `textFromHtml(html)` for the chapter body text (L113) — this is the text written to the library search index. Also `escapeHtml` at L23 (and duplicated in `articleImporters.ts` L70).

No `Worker`/`worker` matches anywhere in `src/` — **the app currently uses zero Web Workers**; all index building and searching run on the main thread.

## 4. Library index — where the search corpus lives

- Path: `src/lib/libraryPaths.ts` L35: `indexText: (root, docId) => join(root, "index", "text", `${docId}.json`)`.
- Content (`src/import/importService.ts` `writeIndex` L153–173): `{ schema: 1, chapters: [{ id, title, order, href, text }] }` — **full per-chapter plain text is stored on disk** (per doc, one JSON). Written at import (L224–225, 287–288); deleted on doc delete (`store/libraryManager.ts` L105); rebuilt from the EPUB by backup reindex (`backup/reindex.ts` L37–78); included in backups (`backup/backupService.ts` L891).
- LibraryScreen builds a fresh in-memory `MiniSearch` from all these files when the search panel opens, only when `searchSignature(rows)` changes (L58–104); each chapter becomes one doc with `id: "${row.id}::${ch.id}"`, doc title as `title/docTitle`, href fallback from `meta.json` for pre-href indexes (L75–85).
- Results UI: inline `.folio-searchbar` / `.folio-searchresults` in LibraryScreen (L335–377); clicking a result calls `openReader({ docId: r.docId, location: r.location ?? null })` (L364). Also triggered by `/` and Ctrl+F (L206–226).

## 5. Worker usage

None. `grep -i worker desktop/src` → 0 matches. (`src-tauri` Rust side is unrelated to search.)

## 6. Tests

- **`tests/miniSearch.test.ts`** (51 lines): pins snippet escaping (script/img injection can't survive into `<mark>` HTML), original casing inside `<mark>`, `href/docTitle/chapterTitle` passthrough, and `escapeHtml` covers exactly `& < > " '`.
- **`tests/searchCache.test.ts`** (31 lines): `searchSignature` is stable across object identity; changes on add/remove/retitle.
- **`tests/inbookSearchPanel.test.tsx`**: count text ("1 match found"), spinner/loading state, clear button, `<mark>Sherlock</mark>` in the card HTML, locator passed to `onSelectResult` (`"text/ch1.xhtml#p4"`), panel closes after a successful selection, no-matches empty state.
- **`tests/reader.test.ts`** L550–621: ReadiumEngine search reuses the cached index across searches, returns empty after destroy, and **retries (rebuilds) after a failed index build** instead of caching the rejection.
- **`tests/locatorCodec.test.ts` / `tests/locatorNavigation.test.ts` / `tests/navigation.test.ts`**: round-trips of `href#frag?p&q&b&a` locators incl. text anchors, and the two-step annotation jump (see §7).

## 7. `goAnchored` / text-anchor locators in the reader

- **`src/reader/ReaderEngine.ts` L96**: `goAnchored?(quote, prefix, suffix): Promise<boolean>` — optional engine method ("second step of two-step jumps").
- **`src/reader/readiumEngine.ts` L205–220**: builds a `Locator` from the *current base locator* + `LocatorText({ highlight: quote, before: prefix, after: suffix })` and calls `nav.go(loc, true)`.
- **`src/reader/navigation.ts` L142–172 `goToAnnotation`**: the only caller — chapter landing first (`engine.go(location)`), then best-effort `goAnchored`; a failed anchor does not fail the navigation.
- **`src/reader/locatorCodec.ts`** (whole file): the persisted locator format `ch1.xhtml?p=0.4286&q=Call%20me&b=pre&a=post#note1`; `LocatorAnchor { quote, prefix?, suffix? }` (L23–27), `MAX_ANCHOR_CHARS = 200` (L39), `decodeLocation` (L92), `anchorOf` (L148), `withAnchor` (L169). `epubcfi(...)` is rejected (L48–50).
- **`src/reader/readiumEngine.ts` L439–469 `locatorFromString`**: rebuilds a Locator from the persisted string; comment at L434–438 explains Readium's `loadLocator` fallback order: **text anchor (`go_text`) → element id → in-resource progression**. The decoded quote is also used for highlight decorations (L464–468 → `applyDecorations` L230–246, which skips unresolvable locators).
- Search results do **not** use any of this — in-book hits carry only a bare chapter href, and library-search hits pass `location` (chapter href, possibly with `#fragment` fallback from meta) straight to `openReader`.

- Four divergent HTML→text paths, only one decodes entities (positions.ts); the reader's in-book corpus keeps raw `&` entities, so searches for words containing entities/typographic chars fail.
- No offsets/positions from MiniSearch — snippets are ad-hoc `indexOf` slices, so in-book jumps can't anchor to the match (chapter-start only).

I now have everything to design. Let me lay out the implementation plan concretely:

## Design

### A. Shared `htmlToText()` — `src/lib/htmlToText.ts`
Pure-string, deterministic, no DOM (works in jsdom + webview; fast for 3MB):
- Strip `<?xml...?>`, comments, and `<script|style|head|title?>` blocks.
- Replace **block-level closing tags** with `" "` (and optionally `\n`?). Callers:
  - `textLengthOfHtml` (positions): collapses whitespace anyway → length only.
  - search corpus (engine): needs text where entities decoded, block boundaries → space, **whitespace collapsed** for tokenization and offsets.

Key decision for **anchoring correctness**: the quote/prefix/suffix passed to `goAnchored` must match what Readium's text-anchor matcher sees. Let me check @readium/navigator's text matching implementation to know its normalization. Let me grep node_modules/@readium for "go_text" / LocatorText matching.

Actually the existing annotation flow: `goToAnnotation` uses quote from `a.quote` which comes from real DOM selection (`selectionFrom`) — exact DOM text. For search, quote from extracted corpus text must match DOM text. If Readium matching is whitespace-normalized + case-insensitive, then a collapsed-whitespace quote works even though DOM textContent has newlines between blocks. If exact, we need extraction that mirrors textContent.

Let me check the navigator source.

### Corpus + offsets
For per-occurrence results I need:
- For each chapter: `text` (extracted), and the ability to find occurrences of the query.
- Snippet: context ±40 chars with `<mark>`.
- Anchor: quote = the matched phrase run (or window ±32? plan: "text-anchored locator (quote ±32 chars) so goAnchored lands on the match") — plan wording: quote with ±32 chars context? Actually plan says "text-anchored locator (quote ±32 chars)". Interpretation: quote = the matched text (maybe with prefix/suffix = ±32 chars context). Use prefix = 32 chars before, suffix = 32 after, highlight = the matched text run. Wait — the highlight must be *findable* in DOM: use the matched words (query text as found in corpus). For multi-word queries spanning collapsed whitespace, quote could contain single spaces where DOM has newlines — again depends on matching tolerance.

So first verify Readium's matching behaviour. Search node_modules/@readium/navigator/dist for "text" matching / normalization.

### MiniSearch upgrade (in-place)
Add:
- `postings: Map<term, Map<docIdx, count>>` (precomputed TF + DF cached implicitly).
- Sorted vocab array + binary search for prefix expansion (find range of terms with prefix).
- `search(query, limit)` with quoted phrase support: `"quick brown"` phrase token → docs containing both tokens adjacent in token stream? Phrase adjacency requires token positions per doc. Store `termPositions: Map<term, Map<docIdx, number[]>>`? That's memory-heavy but the plan asked for "quoted phrase support". Simpler: phrase matching via text indexOf on the normalized text: keep `doc.text` normalized + token offsets? For library index text is stored anyway. For phrase support in candidate selection: phrase = sequence of tokens; candidate docs = AND of tokens; then verify phrase adjacency via token positions stored per doc per term. Store positions only for phrase queries lazily? Simpler: store per-doc token array? Memory: 3MB book → ~600k tokens... heavy but the in-book index is per-book and built lazily; the library index is full corpus of all books — token arrays too heavy.

Alternative pragmatic phrase support: verify phrase by regex on the doc's normalized text (store normalized text per doc — docs already store text; normalizeQuery(text) is deterministic; compute lazily only when phrase query runs). Phrase query: build regex from tokens joined with `\s+` boundary-respecting (token char class) and test each candidate doc's normalized text; snippet uses first match. That's simple and correct.

- Per-occurrence support for in-book: MiniSearch returns hits per *doc*; the engine then expands to occurrences by scanning doc text for query matches (phrase regex first; else each token). Better: keep occurrence scanning in a new module `src/search/occurrences.ts` so it's testable: `findOccurrences(text, query): Array<{start, end, matchText}>` — phrase regex (quoted or multi-token adjacency?) Plan: "all matches per chapter (phrase first, then all-words)". Meaning: if query is a phrase (quoted or natural multi-word?), match phrase occurrences; then fall back to all-words (each word individually, sorted by position). For a 2-word unquoted query "sherlock holmes": phrase-first means find "sherlock holmes" runs; if none, match each word. I'll implement: tokens = tokenize(query); if tokens.length > 1, first pass = phrase (tokens joined with `\s+` in original text, case-insensitive); occurrences of phrase; then for remaining words without a phrase occurrence nearby... Plan says "phrase first, then all-words" — i.e., the *chapter matching* strategy: prefer chapters matching the phrase; then chapters matching all words. For occurrences within a chapter: produce occurrences for the phrase if present, else for each token (all words). Each occurrence = one result.

Simplify occurrences: if phrase present in chapter → occurrences = phrase matches. Else → occurrences = matches of each individual token, sorted by position, capped (say 200/chapter? plan's done-when: 30 occurrences → 30 navigable results; overall cap? Panel groups by chapter with counts. Keep per-chapter cap generous e.g. 100? Or no cap for in-book but limit total results (e.g., 500). For 3MB book, "the" could appear 30k times — need a cap. Use MAX_OCCURRENCES = 200 per book, with per-chapter count shown; if truncated, show "N more" maybe. Keep simple: total cap 300 occurrences, chapters ordered by BM25 score.

- Highlight offsets ("offset map for correct accent/fuzzy/prefix highlights"): MiniSearch snippet currently does indexOf of token in raw text — fails for fuzzy/prefix/accented. Fix: occurrences-based snippets: for each hit doc, use findOccurrences on the doc text (phrase or token-level), snippet from first occurrence with the matched span marked. For multi-token, mark each token occurrence within the window? Keep: snippet marks all token matches within the ±40 window (like browsers). Implement `buildSnippet(text, spans, window=40)` in occurrences.ts — escape + wrap each span.

### Engine changes
`ReaderEngine.search` returns richer hits. Keep interface additive:
```ts
export interface SearchHit {
  chapterTitle: string;
  snippetHtml: string;
  locator: string;          // chapter href (encoded for engine.go)
  anchor?: { quote, prefix, suffix };  // NEW: text anchor to land on the match
  count?: number;  // occurrences in this chapter? (group-level)
}
```
But panel needs *per-occurrence* results: each hit = one occurrence with its own anchor. Group by chapter with counts. So `search` returns flat per-occurrence hits; panel groups adjacent same-chapter hits and shows counts. chapterTitle on each hit; count per chapter = occurrences count in that chapter.

Per-occurrence hit: `{ chapterTitle, snippetHtml, locator: href, anchor: {quote, prefix, suffix}, indexInChapter? }`. Panel: group consecutive hits with same chapterTitle, display chapter header + count + occurrence cards. Actually simpler UI: keep flat list but show chapter header once per group with count badge. Implement grouping in panel render (consecutive same-locator grouping).

Navigation: `onSelectResult` → new coordinator method `goToSearchHit(hit)`: enqueueAbsolute: `engine.go(href)` then `engine.goAnchored(anchor)`. Panel must stay open now (change from current close-on-success!). Tests: existing test expects `closed === true` after selection — must update test (plan changes behavior deliberately).

Current-match counter: hook tracks `activeIndex` (0-based) + total; counter "3 of 41". Next/Prev: Enter/Shift+Enter/F3 (Shift+F3 too?) — plan says Next/Prev (Enter/Shift+Enter/F3). F3 = next; Shift+F3 = prev. Enter from input = next; Shift+Enter = prev. Clicking a result sets activeIndex to that occurrence and navigates.

Temporary decoration for active match: when active hit changes (on navigation), apply decoration group with single spec `{ id: "search-active", locator: withAnchor(href, anchor), style: "highlight", color: accent-ish }`. Use a distinct color e.g. orange? Use accent color `#A7C4A6`-ish... Pick `#FFD59E`? Choose a visible active color: use `--folio-accent-container`-ish. Simplest: `#BFDFF7` blue like selection? For active search match, browsers use orange. Use `#F6C177`-ish? Let's use `#FFB86B`? Hmm, arbitrary; pick `#F5C26B` "search active amber". Cleared on close (and on query change, and on doc reset).

Decoration application needs engine.applyDecorations with full list (annotations + search-active) — the engine effect paints annotations via refreshAnnotations. If I call applyDecorations with only search spec, does it clear previous highlights? `nav.applyDecorations(locators, "highlights")` — Readium's applyDecorations replaces the whole group (group id "highlights"). So mixing would wipe annotations. Need separate group id: applyDecorations API hardcodes "highlights" group. Extend DecorationSpec with optional `group`? Engine method signature `applyDecorations(decorations: DecorationSpec[])` — group param: modify ReadiumEngine.applyDecorations to accept optional group id param (second arg, default "highlights") and add `applySearchDecoration(spec | null)`? Cleaner: add optional `group?: "highlights" | "search"` on DecorationSpec; engine groups by it and calls nav.applyDecorations per group. Keep additive (schema-1 unaffected).

Engine effect in useReaderEngine paints annotations via refreshAnnotations → engine.applyDecorations(decorationsFor(list)) with group default highlights. Search active decoration applied separately with group "search". When only search group is passed, only that group is replaced — annotations preserved. 

But wait: does `applyDecorations(locators, "search")` with empty array clear the group? Readium applyDecorations with empty list for a group should clear. We'll call with [] to clear on close.

### 2-char minimum
Enforce in hook: `if (inbookQuery.trim().length < 2) → no search` (keep panel hint). Also engine.search guards `< 2`.

### Keyboard: F3/Enter/Shift+Enter
- Input onKeyDown in panel: Enter → onNext(), Shift+Enter → onPrev(). F3 anywhere (reader scope, while panel open) → next; Shift+F3 → prev. Wire in useReaderKeyboard: if inbook search open → F3 next etc. The keyboard hook needs access: pass `onSearchNext/onSearchPrev` props? useReaderKeyboard signature takes lots of params; check how it accesses search hook state — earlier hook takes injected callbacks (announceBookmark, setChromeVisible). Look at its param shape later.

### Web Worker
Library search indexing in a worker: `src/search/librarySearchWorker.ts`. Vite handles `new Worker(new URL("./librarySearchWorker.ts", import.meta.url), { type: "module" })`. Worker imports MiniSearch, receives `{type:"index", docs}` posts `{type:"ready"}` or `{type:"progress", done, total}`? Indexing progress: docs arrive in chunks; post progress after each chunk. LibraryScreen: read index/text JSONs (main thread, existing code), then send docs to worker, keep worker alive (per screen mount? create lazily on search open; terminate on unmount?). Simpler: keep a module-level singleton worker; rebuild index by sending docs; worker replies with results for queries `{type:"search", query, limit, token}`.

But tests: vitest jsdom — Worker not available (jsdom has no Worker). Guard: `typeof Worker !== "undefined"` fallback to main-thread index (same code path used in tests and jsdom). LibraryScreen uses a `SearchClient` abstraction: `src/search/searchClient.ts` with worker + fallback. Hmm, this adds complexity. The plan demands worker; implement with graceful fallback.

In-book index worker: engine builds corpus via `pub.get(link).read()` (main thread, needed), then tokenization+indexing in worker. Engine search flow: build corpus array (main), send to worker, query → occurrences computed... occurrences need doc text; worker returns matching doc ids + which occurrences? The occurrence scan needs text + query; could run in worker too and return occurrences with spans + snippets (HTML-safe escape in worker, fine). Then engine maps to hits. Worker holds the corpus (texts) + index for the book lifetime. But worker lifecycle per engine instance; destroy → terminate. Tests use jsdom (no Worker) → fallback to synchronous path. Refactor: core pure functions `buildSearchIndex(docs)` + `searchOccurrences(index, query, opts)` used by both worker and sync fallback.

This is a big chunk. Also library indexing with progress: worker posts progress during addAll; LibraryScreen can show "Indexing N/M…" — check existing UI state in LibraryScreen (searchIndexRef building flag). Keep: emit progress via callback into store state `searchIndexProgress`? LibraryScreen local state showing "Indexing…" in search panel.

### perf
Add search benchmark to scripts/perf.ts: generate ~3MB text corpus, build index, measure index time + search time; assert budget? The done-when: "3 MB book <100 ms after index" refers to search being fast after index. Add `perf search` measurements printed; on Linux record numbers. Keep budgets: index build ≤ 2s? search <100ms.

### Order of implementation
1. `src/lib/htmlToText.ts` + fixture + tests; migrate positions.ts, readiumEngine stripHtml, sanitize.textFromHtml, epubImporter (via textFromHtml already).
2. `src/search/occurrences.ts` (findOccurrences, buildSnippet) + tests.
3. MiniSearch upgrade (postings/TF/DF cache, sorted vocab + binary prefix, phrase support, occurrences-based snippet) + tests (existing miniSearch tests keep passing; add phrase/fuzzy/prefix highlight tests).
4. Engine: per-occurrence search + anchor on hits + search decoration group; ReaderEngine types.
5. Hook + panel: stays open, grouping + counts, "x of N", next/prev, active decoration; keyboard F3.
6. Worker for library search + progress + fallback.
7. Perf bench + docs + gates.

Given the volume, let me start with 1–3 (pure functions + tests), then engine/UI.
